AIApprovalAbout: Which steps wait for your OK.
AIApprovalBanner: The AI task is waiting for your approval.
AIApprovalNoteHere: Moving your mouse pauses the AI at once.
AIApprovalNoteThere: Moving the mouse on {device} pauses the AI at once.
AIAskHere: What should the AI do on this computer?
AIAskHereAbout: It sees this screen and uses the mouse and keyboard. Moving your mouse pauses it at once.
AIAskThere: What should the AI do on {device}?
AIAskThereAbout: It sees {device}'s screen and uses its mouse and keyboard, with {device}'s own AI provider and key.
AIBusyHere: This computer is working on another task.
AIChatNote: Needs a model that accepts images and calls tools; Kyokai offers its actions as tools.
AIDoUnknown: An action that could not be read
AIDoZoom: Look closer at part of the screen
AIHintSend: Enter to send · Shift+Enter for a new line
AIHintSendShift: Shift+Enter to send · Enter for a new line
AIKeyStored: A key is stored. Leave this empty to keep it.
AILinkConfirming: Waiting for {device} to allow AI tasks…
AIModelID: model id, as the provider names it
AINoModelsListed: The provider listed no models that can operate a desktop.
AINotifyApprovalBody: Allow or deny its next action in Kyokai.
AIRecentAbout: This computer's tasks and your sessions with other devices, which a new session lists.
AIRemoteBanner: An AI task from {device} is working on this computer.
AIRestartHint: Start again with a new instruction
AISendKeyAbout: In an AI session's prompt box.
AISetUpFirst: Choose a model with a key in Settings › AI first.
AIStatePausedLocal: Paused because you used the keyboard or mouse
AIStatePausedSleep: Paused: the computer went to sleep
AISuggestThree: Find last month's invoice and print it
AIWhoMay: Who may run AI tasks here
AIWhoMayAbout: Set in Access: Run AI tasks and Approve AI actions. They use these providers, never their own keys.
AIWorkingHint: Working — pause or stop the task to write
AppUpdateInstallFailed: The update could not be installed.
AppUpdateUnavailable: This copy of Kyokai cannot update itself.
BackupAbout: Into a file locked with a passphrase you choose.
BackupHint: A backup keeps this Device ID, the permanent password, trusted devices and known devices, encrypted with a passphrase of at least 10 characters. Without the passphrase it can't be opened.
ByAddressAbout: By IP address or domain name, on port 47310. A password or your OK is still needed.
ByAddressFailed: Not accepting yet: port 47310 is in use or blocked on this computer.
ByAddressHint: Other devices can connect by this computer's IP address or domain name (port 47310), without a network. They still need a password or your confirmation. Windows may ask to let Kyokai through its firewall.
ByAddressRangesHint: Address ranges (192.168.0.0/16) or single addresses, one per line. By default: local networks and Tailscale (100.64.0.0/10). Connections from anywhere else are closed at once.
CleanupHelper: Removed Kyokai Helper and the settings it had left behind: this run mode holds this computer's.
CleanupHelperHasMore: Kyokai Helper on this computer holds devices, networks or a permanent password, and this run mode holds none. Use Kyokai Helper's? Otherwise they are removed with it.
CleanupUserSet: Removed the settings No privileges mode had left behind: Kyokai Helper holds this computer's.
CloseAskTitle: Disconnect from the devices in this window?
ConnectIdentifying: Looking for the device at that address…
ConnectNeedsNetwork: To connect by Device ID, join a network on the Network page first. An IP address or domain name works without one.
EngineDown: The Kyokai engine is not running.
FailAbsent: Nobody is at that computer to allow the connection.
FailBusy: The other device has too many open requests. Try again shortly.
FailHelperOutdated: Kyokai Helper on this device is {helper}, older than this app ({app}). Update it in General, Run mode, then reconnect.
FailIncompatible: That device runs an incompatible version of Kyokai.
FailIncompatibleVersion: That device runs Kyokai {peer} and this one runs {app}: install the same version on both.
FailKeyChanged: That device's identity changed since you last connected. If you expected this, forget the old identity and connect again.
FailRateLimited: Too many attempts. Try again later.
FailTimeout: No one answered on the other device.
FailUnreachable: Couldn't reach that device. Check that it's online in the same network.
FailWrongDevice: A different device answered for that ID.
HelperRestarted: Kyokai Helper restarted with the permissions allowed so far.
HideFromCaptureAbout: Keeps Kyokai's windows out of screenshots, screen sharing and the AI's view.
HomeDevicesNone: Devices you connect to show here.
HomeOthersNone: No other Kyokai device is online in your networks.
HomeOthersNote: {count, plural, =0 {Kyokai devices you haven't connected to} one {Kyokai devices you haven't connected to · #} other {Kyokai devices you haven't connected to · #}}
HomePasswordsOff: No password opens this device: other devices sign in with a key, or ask you. Change it in Permissions.
HomePermanentMissing: No permanent password is set, so no password opens this device. Set one in Permissions.
HomePermanentOnly: Only the permanent password opens this device. Change it in Permissions.
IdentifyBroken: No Kyokai device answered at that address.
IdentifyUnreachable: Nothing answered at that address. Check the address, and that the device accepts connections by address from here.
IdentityFingerprintHint: The full identity behind the Device ID. Compare it when another computer asks you to confirm this device.
IdentityIDAbout: Others use it to reach this computer.
KeysAuthorized: The key can connect to this device now.
KeysFailed: The key could not be made.
KeysMineHint: This device signs in with these keys to other Kyokai devices (Ed25519) and to SSH. Their private parts stay in Kyokai's store and never leave it.
KeysPassphraseOptional: Passphrase for the copy you take (optional)
KeysPastePrivate: Paste a private key (OpenSSH or PEM), or choose its file.
KeysPastePublic: Paste a public key line (ssh-ed25519 …), or choose a .pub file.
KeysSaveFailed: The file could not be written.
KeysShownHint: This private key is shown only now. Copy it or save it to a file; once you choose Done it is gone from this page.
KeysUnreadable: This is not a key Kyokai can read.
KeysUnsupported: Kyokai keeps Ed25519 keys, RSA keys of 2048 bits or more, and ECDSA P-256 or P-384 keys.
NanokvmFound: Found a NanoKVM USB: its capture card and serial port are suggested.
NanokvmHint: A NanoKVM USB plugged into this computer captures another computer's HDMI output and types and points on it through its USB. Choose its capture card and serial port; Kyokai suggests the pair it finds.
NanokvmInUse: {name} is using this NanoKVM USB. Taking over ends their session.
NanokvmOfferAbout: Devices with a correct password or a sign-in key open it without asking, one at a time.
NanokvmSerialAbout: The NanoKVM's keyboard and mouse for the wired computer.
NanokvmVideoAbout: The NanoKVM's HDMI capture: what the wired computer shows.
NetworkDeviceCount: {count, plural, =0 {No Kyokai devices} one {# Kyokai device} other {# Kyokai devices}}
NetworkDevicesHint: A Device ID here is what a device announces. Kyokai checks who a device really is when it connects.
NetworkDirectAbout: Faster where both networks allow it. Off by default.
NetworkDirectHelper: The helper always tries direct connections: its installer allowed it through the firewall.
NetworkDirectHint: Faster when both networks allow it. Windows may ask to let Kyokai through its firewall; while this is off, connections go through the server.
NetworkDirectWarning: This makes Kyokai listen on network ports and answer other devices' packets: Windows Firewall may ask, and other devices on your networks can find this one more easily. It changes what this device exposes, not just a protocol.
NetworkLabelHint: Optional; the network name shows otherwise.
NetworkLatencyFirstHint: Prefer the route with the lowest delay over the one with the fewest hops, in every network.
NetworkEngineAbout: Kyokai Network is built in. The official EasyTier core gives every network its own options.
NetworkEngineHint: EasyTier runs as a program of its own, without a virtual network adapter. It is downloaded from EasyTier's GitHub releases and checked before it runs. Other devices reach this one through it only while no other program uses port 47310 here. easytier-mini is not offered: without a virtual adapter it cannot carry Kyokai's connections.
NetworkEngineBackConfirm:
Kyokai Network cannot use these EasyTier options. They will be removed:

{options}
NetworkOptionsHint: TOML for the official core, for example listeners = ["tcp://0.0.0.0:11010"], or under [flags] enable_kcp_proxy = true. Kyokai sets the servers, network name and secret above, and its own keys, itself.
NetworkUnreachable: other devices can't reach this one
NetworkNone: No network yet. Add one to reach other devices by their Device ID.
NetworkRemoveConfirm: Remove {name}? Kyokai leaves this network and forgets its servers, network name and secret.
NetworkSecretKeep: Leave empty to keep the current secret
NetworkSecretWeak: This network secret is short. Anyone who guesses it can join the network, though joining alone grants no access to this device.
NetworkServersHint: One address per line, for example tcp://example.org:11010
NetworksHint: Join EasyTier networks through standard EasyTier servers, several at once if you like: this device has the same Device ID in each. A device you want to reach by its Device ID joins one of the same networks.
NoLogsAbout: Keeps no logs or record of connections on this computer.
NoLogsConfirm: This is a security risk: afterwards you can't find out who connected to this computer, or which devices it connected to. A device whose key changed is no longer recognized after Kyokai restarts, and a crash leaves nothing to investigate. The logs written so far are deleted.
NoLogsEngineBehind: The engine in use doesn't support this yet; it still keeps logs until it is updated.
NoLogsHint: Kyokai writes no logs or crash reports and keeps no record of connections on this computer: trusted devices and Recent last only until Kyokai quits. Turning it on deletes the logs already written. Reports the system makes itself (macOS crash reports, Windows Error Reporting) are not Kyokai's to stop.
NotifyStillRunningBody: Kyokai keeps running in the tray. Quit it from the tray menu.
PanePopOut: Open in a window of its own
PaneNoRoomAcrossHint: No room side by side: make the window wider
PaneNoRoomDownHint: No room above and below: make the window taller
PasswordGrantsNote: Anything else waits for your OK
PermUseNanokvm: Use the computer wired to its NanoKVM USB
PermUseVNC: Connect to its VNC or Screen Sharing
PermanentSetAbout: Set. Stays the same until you change it.
PermissionAccessibilityHint: Lets other devices and AI tasks use the mouse and keyboard here.
PermissionInputMonitoringHint: Lets Kyokai notice when you use your own keyboard and mouse, so that an AI task pauses and Control+Option+Shift+Esc stops it.
PermissionKeychainHint: Keeps this device's identity, passwords and network settings between starts. Without it, Kyokai keeps them only until it quits and the Device ID changes.
PermissionScreenHint: Lets other devices and AI tasks see this screen.
PermissionsHelperHint: In this run mode the helper captures and controls this Mac: allow these for Kyokai Helper, then restart it here.
PermissionsHint: macOS asks you before an app may record the screen or control the computer. Without these, other devices see a placeholder picture and cannot use the mouse or keyboard here. A permission you allow counts once Kyokai is reopened.
PickThisComputerKvm: The NanoKVM USB plugged in here
PickThisComputerNote: Runs here, with this computer's providers
ProtectedAbout: Leaves only AI settings and tasks until the permanent password turns it off.
ProtectedConfirm: Kyokai will show only the AI settings and AI tasks. To change anything else, you'll need the permanent password to turn protected mode off. Connection requests and devices connected here still show, so you can always deny and disconnect them.
ProtectedHint: This computer's Kyokai then offers only the AI settings and AI tasks; everything else, including the network, permissions and security, stays hidden until the permanent password turns it off. Needs a permanent password.
ProtectedNeedsPermanent: Set a permanent password in Access first.
ProtectedOnHint: Only the AI settings and AI tasks are available. Enter the permanent password to turn protected mode off.
ProtectedWrongPassword: That is not the permanent password.
RenameHint: Shown only on this device. Leave it empty to use the name the device gives itself.
RequestGone: That request is no longer open.
RequestNewKey: This Device ID was used before by another key. It may be a different device claiming it — allow only if you expected this.
RequestNotify: Open Kyokai to allow or deny it.
RequestPermissionsMissing: macOS hasn't allowed Kyokai to record this screen or use the mouse and keyboard yet, so this device can't do all it asks. Allow them under Privacy permissions on Home.
ResetAbout: A new Device ID; trusted and known devices are forgotten.
ResetConfirm: This device gets a new Device ID. Other devices will see it as a new device, and its permanent password, trusted devices and known devices are forgotten. This can't be undone without a backup.
ResetHint: Gives this device a new Device ID and forgets its permanent password, trusted devices and known devices.
RestoreConfirm: This device takes on the identity in the backup, including its Device ID. Every session ends and the network reconnects.
RoutesAddHint: IP address or domain name, port optional
RoutesFailed: The routes could not be changed. Check the address.
RoutesHint: Kyokai reaches this device through the Kyokai network and these IP addresses or domain names. Auto takes the best at every connection, by its delay now and how well it went before; a route chosen by hand is used alone.
RunModeBackgroundAbout: The helper also lets devices in before anyone signs in.
RunModeFollowAbout: While Kyokai runs, a helper that can also show and use sign-in and administrator prompts.
RunModeKept: Nothing was moved: each run mode keeps its own identity.
RunModeMovedHint: Its Device ID, networks and saved passwords moved to Kyokai Helper, which is not installed now. Install it again to get them back, or start over here with a new identity.
RunModeMovedStartOverConfirm: Start over with a new Device ID? Devices that knew this computer will see a new one, and its networks and saved passwords have to be set up again.
RunModeMovedTitle: This computer's identity is in Kyokai Helper
RunModeNote: Follow Kyokai and Background service install a helper once, after one administrator prompt; with Background service the permanent password also lets a device in before anyone signs in (while Connect without asking is on). Your Device ID, trusted devices and settings move with it.
RunModeOutdated: The helper is {helper}; this app is {app}.
RunModeReplaceIdentity: The other run mode holds another identity of this computer, with its own settings. Replace it with this one? Its Device ID, networks and saved passwords are then gone.
RunModeUnavailable: Only No privileges is available on this system yet.
RunModeUserAbout: Runs inside Kyokai itself. Nothing to install.
SavedHint: What this device keeps to sign in to others. Only that something is kept shows here, never a password.
SecretsDenied: Access to the Keychain was denied: secrets are kept only until Kyokai quits. Allow it under Privacy permissions.
SecretsMemoryOnly: In memory only: this computer's credential store is not available, so the Device ID changes on the next start.
SecretsOSStore: Encrypted with this computer's credential store
SecretsUnreadable: The saved identity cannot be unlocked. Kyokai uses a temporary one this time and leaves the saved one untouched.
ServiceDown: That service is not running on the other device.
ServiceFailed: The connection could not be opened.
ServiceHostKeyChanged: This device's SSH key is not the one it had before. Kyokai sent no password. Trust the new key only if you know why it changed.
ServiceKeyHint: Signs in with this device's keys (Security, Your keys). The server must list one of them in that user's authorized_keys.
ServiceNeedsSignIn: This server needs a sign-in. Choose another way to sign in.
ServiceNoAnswer: The server did not answer the sign-in. After failed sign-ins a server can hold new ones for several minutes: wait a few minutes, check the user name and password, then reconnect.
ServiceNoTunnel: That device runs an older Kyokai: update it there to reach its services.
ServiceNoneHint: For a VNC server that asks for no password.
ServicePortsHint: Where SSH, Remote Desktop and VNC listen on this computer. Another device only chooses the service: Kyokai connects it to the port set here. Leave a field empty for the standard port.
ServicePortsInvalid: A port is a number from 1 to 65535.
ServiceReplaced: Someone else signed in to that desktop, so this connection ended.
ServiceScreenHint: The other computer's own sign-in screen asks once connected (Network Level Authentication must be off there).
ServiceSignInHint: Choose how to sign in to {service} on that device. With Remember, Kyokai signs in the same way next time, and asks again only if that fails.
ServiceVNCLoopback: The VNC server closed the connection at once. It may refuse connections from its own computer: on that computer, turn on “Allow loopback connections” (TightVNC) or AllowLoopback (UltraVNC).
ServiceVNCUnsupported: That VNC server asks for a kind of sign-in Kyokai does not support. On that computer, turn on VNC password authentication (RealVNC Server: VNC password, with encryption allowed off; UltraVNC: MS-Logon off).
ServiceWrongSignIn: The user name or password was not accepted.
SessionConfirmingHere: Waiting for you to allow it
SessionConfirmingThere: Waiting for the other device to allow it…
SettingsAboutAI: AI tasks on this computer use its own providers and keys, which never go to other devices.
SettingsAboutAbout: Kyokai's version, updates, and what helps when something goes wrong.
SettingsAboutAccess: Who can connect to this computer, and what they can do.
SettingsAboutGeneral: Language, look, and how Kyokai starts and closes.
SettingsAboutNetwork: How this computer finds your other devices.
SettingsAboutRunMode: Where Kyokai runs on this computer, and what it can reach.
SettingsAboutSecurity: This computer's identity, your keys, and what Kyokai keeps.
SettingsCheckAppUpdatesHint: Only signed updates from Kyokai's GitHub releases are offered.
SettingsAutoInstallHint: Kyokai restarts into a new version only while nothing is connected, no request waits and no AI task runs. Idle: nobody has used this computer for 15 minutes.
SettingsCloseButtonAbout: What the window's close button does.
SettingsHideFromCaptureConfirm: People who see or control this device will see Kyokai's windows, and those controlling it can use them: change its settings and passwords, start AI tasks or answer in your place. Kyokai's AI never can, and nobody can while a connection request or an AI approval waits for you.
SettingsHideFromCaptureHint: On: Kyokai's windows stay out of screenshots, screen sharing, remote-desktop tools, Kyokai's own video and the AI's screenshots, and the people controlling this device can't use them. Off: they see Kyokai's windows and can use them, for example on an unattended computer; Kyokai's AI never can, and nobody can while a connection request or an AI approval waits for you.
SettingsLanguageAbout: Follows the system unless you choose one.
SettingsNameAbout: What others see beside the Device ID.
SettingsNameHint: What other devices see beside this Device ID once their login succeeded. Leave it empty to use this computer's name.
SettingsNamePublishAbout: Devices in your networks see the name before connecting.
SettingsNamePublishHint: Kyokai devices in the networks this computer joined see its friendly name beside its Device ID, even those that never connected here. Anyone in those networks can see it, and it proves nothing: the Device ID and the sign-in decide.
SettingsOpenAtLoginHint: Off unless you turn it on: Kyokai never starts by itself.
SettingsSoundSourceHint: What devices that control this one hear: what this computer plays, or an input such as a microphone.
SettingsStartHidden: Start in the tray when opened at login
SettingsStartHiddenAbout: Opened at login, Kyokai shows only its tray icon.
SettingsThemeAbout: The button at the bottom of the sidebar switches it too.
SidebarOwnWindow: In a window of its own
SignInKeysAbout: {count, plural, one {# key can sign in instead of a password.} other {# keys can sign in instead of a password.}}
SignInKeysNone: No key can sign in yet.
SignInNone: Nothing is checked: every connection asks you, and with nobody at this computer no one gets in.
SignInPermanentMissing: Not set yet. Set one to use it.
SignInTemporaryAbout: Shown on Home. Changes each time Kyokai starts.
SoundSourceAbout: What devices controlling this one hear.
SplitCameApart: {group} didn't fit on this display, so its {count} panes each have their own entry now.
StartOverDone: This device has a new identity, kept from now on.
StartOverHint: Without a backup it cannot come back. Start over to keep a new identity from now on; the old file stays aside, untouched.
StatusNoCredential: Save a password or a key for this device to see its status here.
StatusRefused: That device does not share its status with this one.
StatusUnsupported: Its status shows once that device runs Kyokai 0.4.1 or later.
TourAIApprove: A step that needs you waits for Allow, here or from whoever you let approve.
TourAIBody: Add an AI provider, and an AI task works on this computer's screen, for you or for someone you let in.
TourAIKey: The provider's key stays on this computer and goes only to that provider.
TourAILater: Settings › AI providers, when you like
TourAIPause: Touch the keyboard or mouse and the task pauses at once.
TourAgainAbout: What Kyokai does and how far others reach, step by step.
TourArtAllowed: {count, plural, one {# of 4 allowed} other {# of 4 allowed}}
TourArtDisplay: A display or a dummy plug attached
TourArtGrants: What a correct password lets in
TourArtPanes: Every connection opens as a pane, beside others if you like.
TourArtPrompts: Administrator prompts and the lock screen
TourArtPromptsMac: Password prompts and the lock screen
TourArtReach: What others can see and use
TourArtSignInScreen: The sign-in screen, before anyone signs in
TourArtYourDesktop: Your desktop, while you're signed in
TourAwakeBody: Asleep, this computer is offline in every run mode: nobody reaches it until it wakes.
TourAwakeLinux1: In your desktop's power settings, set the computer to never suspend while plugged in.
TourAwakeLinux2: The screen may turn off or lock: someone connecting turns it on.
TourAwakeMac1: In System Settings › Energy, turn on Prevent automatic sleeping when the display is off (on a MacBook: Battery › Options).
TourAwakeMac2: The display may sleep: only the Mac needs to stay awake, and it works without a display attached.
TourAwakeWin1: In Settings › System › Power, set the computer to never sleep while plugged in.
TourAwakeWin2: The screen may turn off: Kyokai turns it on when someone connects.
TourAwayBackground: From start-up, before anyone signs in, for a computer nobody sits at. Only the permanent password or a key gets in then.
TourAwayBody: Choose how far others can reach. It takes effect when you finish; Settings › Run mode changes it any time.
TourAwayFollow: Also administrator prompts and the lock screen, while Kyokai runs.
TourAwayHelperMac: On a Mac, Kyokai Helper then asks for its own Screen Recording and Accessibility.
TourAwayTitle: When nobody is at this computer
TourAwayUser: Your desktop while you're signed in. The usual choice.
TourConnectBody: On Home, type the other device's Device ID, or an address, and choose Connect. Open as chooses what opens.
TourConnectChecked: Being in the same network grants nothing: every connection signs in, or its user says yes.
TourDirectAskLinux: A firewall (ufw, firewalld) may need its port opened.
TourDirectAskMac: macOS may ask to let Kyokai find devices on the local network.
TourDirectAskWin: Windows may ask to let Kyokai through its firewall.
TourDirectListens: This computer listens for connections and is easier to find.
TourDirectOff: Off until you switch on Try direct connections in Settings › Network.
TourDirectYes: Faster, where both networks allow it.
TourDisplayBody: With no monitor attached, Windows has no screen to show. Leave a monitor connected, or plug in a display emulator (an HDMI or DisplayPort dummy plug). Without either, connect through Remote Desktop, or install a virtual display driver.
TourDisplayBodyLinux: At the sign-in screen there is no desktop to share yet. Stay signed in and lock the screen, or turn on automatic sign-in. On Wayland the desktop asks once whether Kyokai may share the screen.
TourDisplayTitle: Windows needs a display to share
TourDisplayTitleLinux: Linux shares the desktop someone is signed in to
TourKindAI: An AI task that runs there, with that computer's provider and key; its user is asked first.
TourKindDesktop: Its screen, mouse and keyboard, clipboard, files and sound.
TourKindRDP: Windows' own Remote Desktop to it, carried by Kyokai.
TourKindSSH: A terminal on its own SSH server, carried by Kyokai: nothing opened to the internet.
TourKindVNC: Its VNC server, a Mac's Screen Sharing too, carried by Kyokai.
TourLetInBody: Others reach this computer by its Device ID. What they may do depends on how they sign in.
TourLoginOff: Off: others reach this computer once you open Kyokai.
TourLoginOn: Kyokai waits in the tray after you sign in.
TourLoginService: The service runs from start-up anyway; this opens the window too.
TourNetworkBody: Devices find each other through EasyTier networks. Whoever runs yours gives you its servers, its name and its secret.
TourNetworkLater: No network yet? You can still connect by address, or add one later.
TourOpenAI: Open AI providers when I finish
TourOpenAIAbout: Claude and OpenAI are there already; many more are a click away.
TourPasswordNote: The temporary password changes every time Kyokai starts; give it only to someone you want to let in.
TourPrivacyBody: macOS lets Kyokai share this screen and take input only with your permission. Allow… opens the right page of System Settings.
TourPrivacyLater: One you skip stays on Home under Privacy permissions until you allow it.
TourReadyAuthLinux: Here's what you chose. Linux asks once for an administrator's password to install Kyokai Helper.
TourReadyAuthMac: Here's what you chose. macOS asks once for an administrator's password to install Kyokai Helper.
TourReadyAuthWin: Here's what you chose. Windows asks once for an administrator's approval to install Kyokai Helper.
TourReadyUser: Here's what you chose. Nothing needs an administrator.
TourReplayOther: This computer runs in {current}. You looked at {chosen}: Switch changes to it.
TourReplayTitle: How this computer is set up
TourSkipBody: Kyokai starts with No privileges, which needs no administrator. Settings › General can show the tour again.
TourViaServerNote: Slower when the server is far from both of you.
TourViaServerYes: Works on any network; nothing on this computer listens for connections.
TourWelcomeBody: See and use another computer as if you sat at it. An AI can work on a computer for its user too, always on that computer, with that computer's own provider key.
TourWelcomeNote: About two minutes. Nothing changes until you choose it, and Settings › General can show this again.
TourWithNo: No AI tasks, sound or services unless you allow them in Access.
TourWithYes: In at once, with the screen, mouse and keyboard, clipboard and files.
TourWithoutAsk: A request shows who it is and what it asks for. Turn off what you don't want to give, then Allow, or Deny.
TourYouWin: Your own keyboard and mouse always win, over theirs and over any AI.
TrustedHint: Devices you allowed before. A removed device shows as new the next time.
ViewerAIHostApproves: The other computer's user approves this step.
ViewerAsleep: The screen there may be asleep.
ViewerByAddressHint: Connected by address, outside the Kyokai network.
ViewerClipBehind: Not shared right now: another tab or the Kyokai tab is in front.
ViewerClipHint: Only the device whose tab is in front shares the clipboard. What crossed is listed here until the tab closes, and kept nowhere else.
ViewerClipShare: Share the clipboard with this device
ViewerClipboardNoText: The clipboard has no text to type.
ViewerHostAgent: Kyokai Helper is getting ready there. Trying again…
ViewerHostAsleep: The screen there is asleep. Waking it…
ViewerHostCannotCapture: That computer can't share its screen.
ViewerHostDark: The screen there is off. Waking it…
ViewerHostNanokvm: The NanoKVM's capture card on that computer isn't available.
ViewerHostNoCodec: This device can't show the picture that computer sends.
ViewerHostNoDisplay: The computer there shows no screen right now. Trying again…
ViewerHostRetrying: The picture there could not start. Trying again…
ViewerInputPaused: Input paused — the connection is behind
ViewerKeyboardGrabBehind: Keyboard: another window is in front of Kyokai's, so the keys stay there.
ViewerKeyboardGrabMissed: Keyboard: some keys got past Kyokai; it sent them itself and took the keyboard again.
ViewerKeyboardGrabNoReader: Keyboard: Kyokai is not reading the keys right now; they go as in Legacy meanwhile.
ViewerKeyboardGrabOff: Keyboard: move the pointer into this pane to send every key to the device.
ViewerKeyboardGrabRenewing: Keyboard: the system stopped handing the keys to Kyokai; it is taking the keyboard again.
ViewerKeyboardGrabSecure: Keyboard: another app has secure keyboard entry on, so macOS keeps the keys from Kyokai; they go as in Legacy meanwhile.
ViewerKeyboardGrabSecureBy: Keyboard: {app} has secure keyboard entry on, so macOS keeps the keys from Kyokai; they go as in Legacy meanwhile.
ViewerKeyboardGrabTaking: Keyboard: every key goes to the device.
ViewerKeyboardNoGrab: Allow Accessibility for Kyokai in System Settings to send every key, then reopen this connection.
ViewerNoDecoder: The picture can't be shown: Kyokai's core library is missing.
ViewerNoPicture: This session does not show the screen.
ViewerPlaceholder: The other device can't record its screen yet: this is a placeholder picture.
ViewerPointerHint: Marks where their pointer is, for computers whose picture leaves it out.
ViewerRelayedHint: The connection goes through the server. For a faster path, turn on Try direct connections (Network) on both devices.
ViewerSoundHint: Plays what the other computer plays. Remembered for this device.
ViewerTimes: The other computer takes {encode} ms to encode, the network {network} ms; this one takes {decode} ms to decode and {draw} ms to draw. {fps} frames a second, up to {target}.
ViewerUnsupported: This picture uses {codec}, which this version can't show yet.
WatchersHint: These devices show this computer's processor, memory, disk and network use on their Home page. Turn off “See this computer's status” above to stop them.
WatchersNone: No device is watching this computer's status.
WithoutAskingAbout: Off: you allow each connection yourself.
WithoutAskingHint: A way to sign in checked above lets a device in with what passwords grant, without asking you. With nobody at this computer (Background service), only the permanent password or a key does. Off: you are always asked.
